method: Runs use the actual CodeSearch.Service, not a copy of its ranking algorithm.
The baseline loads committed search code against the current checkout's dependencies and corpus.
The pinned embedding model was cached before these runs. Yolk was enabled.
Each process builds its index, then runs all queries three times.
Benchmark processes run sequentially. First-pass and repeated-query timings are separate.
Memory deltas measure the cold build after full garbage collection before and after indexing.
Peak RSS measures the whole process. RSS deltas can vary with initial memory and allocator behavior.
Gold paths identify intended implementations. Other valid answers can count as misses.
Existing source and benchmark files can contain the tuning queries. Held-out queries live in unindexed JSON.
These are local measurements, not statistical confidence intervals.
observations: Compact numeric postings preserved all original tuning ranks before ranking changes.
Per-file term sets replace duplicated per-document frequency maps. Deleted documents release their metadata.
Semantic expansion keeps only six candidates per word instead of sorting the whole vocabulary.
The expansion cache holds at most 128 queries and invalidates after corpus changes.
Smaller expansion weights and path hints reduce unrelated vendor and test matches without excluding those files.
File-hint precomputation preserved all reported ranks and first-result paths in both modes.
The server route composition query recovered its target at rank 8 semantically and rank 7 offline.
Semantic ripgrep file enumeration regressed from rank 1 to rank 2. No held-out ranks regressed.
HTTP API server routes and the effect-based client API query still miss their gold targets in the top ten.
Semantic RSS delta increased, but retained heap and whole-process peak RSS decreased.
The final candidate passed 13 search tests, 26 assertions, and Core typechecking.
